purpose: How a licensed Medicare-focused insurance agent decides which credentials, carrier contracts, and consumer permissions must be in force before any prospect is contacted, which marketing, event, and lead-generation activity is permitted under the overlapping federal, state, carrier, and upline rule layers of the current plan year, how the duty owed to an older or impaired beneficiary constrains every one of those choices, and what evidence each activity must leave behind so the practice survives a carrier audit, a secret shop, a regulator inquiry, or a complaint investigation.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the operator is an independent licensed producer or small agency contracted with several carriers, not a carrier employee, not a captive call center, and not a government or SHIP counselor

the governing rules are re-issued on an annual plan-year cycle and differ by state, by carrier, and by upline, so every specific threshold, interval, retention period, and dollar limit named here is a class of obligation to verify in current-year sources for the agent's own jurisdiction, never a fact to rely on from memory
compensation for enrollments and renewals is set by regulated schedules and carrier contracts; it is treated here only as a mechanism that must never influence which plan a beneficiary is shown

the material is educational and operational for the agent's own practice; it is not legal, tax, medical, or personalized insurance advice, and questions of legal interpretation are routed to licensed counsel and to the carrier's compliance desk
exclusions: the enrollment-period calendar, plan comparison, coverage-type trade-offs, drug and network fit, and the enrollment conversation itself, all of which belong to the sibling enrollment-periods-and-plan-fit knowledge base

renewal compensation mechanics, year-round service work, annual-review practice, retention, and book growth through referrals, all of which belong to the sibling renewal-compensation-and-retention knowledge base

any personalized recommendation of a specific plan to a specific beneficiary; plan selection is the beneficiary's decision and this knowledge base only governs how the agent may lawfully reach and inform them

stating specific commission amounts, override percentages, gift-value thresholds, waiting-period lengths, retention periods, or continuing-education hours as fact; all such figures are described as mechanisms whose current values must be verified per jurisdiction, carrier, and plan year
clinical judgement about a beneficiary's conditions, medications, or providers, and any legal interpretation of a statute or regulation, both of which are outside an agent's licence

competency_questions.question: Which credentials, certifications, and contracts must be in force before I may market or enroll anyone this plan year, and how do I verify each one is actually current rather than assumed current?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REGULATORY_OPERATING_FRAME names the rule layers, STATE_LICENSE_AND_CE and ANNUAL_CERTIFICATION_CYCLE state the credential classes and their calendars, and READY_TO_SELL_VERIFICATION gives the per-carrier verification that gates activity

competency_questions.question: How do I decide whether a growth idea is allowed at all, and what do I do when no compliant version of it exists?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPLIANCE_OVER_GROWTH_RULE supplies the written pre-approval gate and the abandon-and-substitute path, and PROHIBITED_PRACTICE_CATALOG supplies the list the idea is checked against

competency_questions.question: What does the annual certification cycle actually require, in what order should I complete it, and what happens to my season if I miss a carrier's window?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ANNUAL_CERTIFICATION_CYCLE sequences the shared annual training ahead of per-carrier product modules and names the attempt-limit and deadline classes to verify, and READY_TO_SELL_VERIFICATION states the consequence of an incomplete certification

competency_questions.question: How should I structure my carrier contracts and my upline hierarchy, and what will it cost me to move a contract later?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CARRIER_CONTRACTING_AND_EO covers the contract stack, portfolio breadth, and errors-and-omissions class, and HIERARCHY_AND_RELEASE_MECHANICS explains release and dormancy as the mobility mechanism to confirm in writing before signing

competency_questions.question: When may I contact a prospect at all, what counts as permission, which regime does it come from, and how long does it last?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PERMISSION_TO_CONTACT separates the Medicare marketing, telephone-consumer, and carrier documentation regimes and states the scope-and-expiry discipline, and CONSENT_AND_CONTACT_RECORDS states what artifact must exist

competency_questions.question: What must be agreed and documented before a personal appointment, and what may and may not be discussed once I am in the room?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCOPE_OF_APPOINTMENT gives the pre-appointment scope artifact, its timing and retention classes, and the re-papering rule, and EDUCATION_VS_ADVICE_LINE bounds what may be claimed and how a personal question is handled

competency_questions.question: Which marketing practices are flatly prohibited and which are permitted only with conditions attached?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROHIBITED_PRACTICE_CATALOG separates the absolute prohibitions from the conditional classes and stores each condition next to its practice, and EVENT_COMPLIANCE_CLASSES applies the distinction to event conduct

competency_questions.question: Before any flyer, page, post, or advertisement goes public, what review, disclosure, and versioning does it need?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKETING_MATERIAL_REVIEW gives the plan-specific versus general distinction, the submission path, the disclosure classes, and plan-year versioning, and DIGITAL_PRESENCE_COMPLIANCE adds the durability, targeting, and public-comment problems unique to online assets

competency_questions.question: How do I run an educational or a sales event without turning presence-building into a violation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVENT_COMPLIANCE_CLASSES distinguishes the two event classes with their reporting, advertising, and conduct envelopes, and COMMUNITY_EDUCATION_PRESENCE shows how permission and referrals arrive as a byproduct rather than a pitch

competency_questions.question: How do I buy or generate leads without inheriting somebody else's compliance failure, and how do I keep one channel from being able to end my season?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TPMO_AND_LEAD_VENDOR_RULES gives the vendor diligence and disclaimer, recording, and consent-artifact obligations, and LEAD_SOURCE_PORTFOLIO gives the three-axis source scoring and the diversification rule

competency_questions.question: What extra care do I owe an older, grieving, or impaired prospect, who may sign, and when must I stop the conversation entirely?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VULNERABLE_CONSUMER_DUTY states the pacing, comprehension-check, authority-verification, and hard-stop rules plus the banned pressure tactics, and EDUCATION_VS_ADVICE_LINE keeps the agent out of deciding for the beneficiary

competency_questions.question: What exactly must be in a prospect or client file, how is health and identity data handled, and how fast can I produce a complete file on request?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AUDIT_READY_FILE_STANDARD enumerates the required file contents and the retrieval-under-pressure test, CONSENT_AND_CONTACT_RECORDS covers the permission and recording artifacts, and PRIVACY_AND_PHI_HANDLING covers minimum-necessary handling, storage, and incident response

competency_questions.question: What do I do on the day a complaint, a secret-shop finding, or a carrier investigation lands on me?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPLAINT_AND_ALLEGATION_RESPONSE gives the arrival channels, the same-day triage, the pull-the-file rule, the beneficiary-first correction, and the root-cause record, and SELF_AUDIT_CADENCE closes the finding into a practice change

competency_questions.question: How do I keep the whole compliance stack current as rules, carriers, and my own footprint change from one plan year to the next?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SELF_AUDIT_CADENCE defines the recurring sweeps and the remediation log, REGULATORY_OPERATING_FRAME carries the re-verification dates, and MARKETING_MATERIAL_REVIEW supplies the plan-year purge and re-version pass

glossary.definition: A carrier's own composite finding that a specific agent may market and enroll a specific product in a specific state right now, computed from active licence, in-force appointment, passed current-year certification, and a contract in good standing; it can flip to false without notice when any single input lapses, which is why it is verified from the carrier portal rather than remembered.

The yearly obligation class combining an industry-standard Medicare and fraud-waste-abuse training course (commonly the AHIP-class course) with each carrier's own product and compliance modules, all of which must be passed before that carrier grants selling authority for the coming plan year; accepted courses, attempt limits, and deadlines differ by carrier and must be verified each cycle.

The documented consent that authorizes the agent to reach a specific beneficiary about specific product types through specific channels for a bounded time; several regimes stack here, including the Medicare marketing rule class on unsolicited contact, the telephone-consumer class governing calls, texts, and do-not-call scrubbing, and each carrier's documentation standard.

The documented agreement, captured before a personal marketing appointment, recording which product types the beneficiary agrees to discuss; current rules impose a required interval between the agreement and the appointment with narrow exceptions, a set of required elements, and a retention obligation, all of which are verified per plan year.

The rule class covering entities that generate, sell, or handle Medicare leads and marketing on behalf of agents or plans; agents who buy from or act as one inherit disclaimer, consent-provenance, and call-recording obligations and are held responsible by carriers for how a purchased lead was produced.

The regulatory distinction between content that promotes or influences an enrollment decision for specific plans, which generally carries filing, approval, and disclaimer obligations, and general informational content that does not; the classification determines the review path a piece must take before it exists in public.

Two separately governed event classes: an educational event is advertised as educational, teaches how coverage works, and excludes plan-specific sales activity and application collection, while a marketing or sales event presents plans and may take enrollments under its own conduct, reporting, and advertising rules.

The channel by which a beneficiary complaint made to a plan or to Medicare reaches the carrier and then the agent as an allegation requiring a documented, time-bounded response; the class of record it creates tends to follow an agent across carrier relationships, which is why response quality matters more than argument.

The carrier-controlled mechanism that permits an agent to move an existing carrier contract from one upline hierarchy to another; where a release is refused, the contract typically remains in place until a carrier-defined dormancy period elapses, so the release policy is the term to obtain in writing before signing anything.

The category of promotional item or refreshment that may lawfully be offered without becoming an enrollment inducement, bounded by a value limit set in current-year rules and never conditioned on enrolling; meals at sales events sit outside this class entirely, and the current limit and definitions must be verified rather than remembered.

nodes.definition: Build and maintain the written map of the four overlapping rule sets an agent actually operates under - the federal Medicare marketing and communication rules, the insurance code and producer-conduct rules of every state in the footprint, each contracted carrier's own marketing policy and contract terms, and any upline or field-marketing-organization policy layered on top - and adopt the strictest-applicable-rule habit instead of reasoning from whichever source is most convenient. The unit of work is naming, for each class of activity (initiating contact, holding an appointment, publishing a piece, hosting an event, keeping a record), which layer governs it and exactly where the current-year text of that rule lives, so every later decision resolves to a named source with a verification date rather than to memory or to what an upline said on a call. The map is deliberately a living artifact because these rule sets are re-issued annually and diverge by state and by carrier; it carries an explicit instruction to re-read the current-year rules in the agent's own jurisdiction before relying on any specific interval, threshold, or dollar limit.

included: the four governing rule layers and which activity class each governs
the strictest-applicable-rule resolution habit
a named current-year locator and verification date per obligation class
excluded: legal interpretation of any regulation, which belongs to licensed counsel
plan benefit design and comparison, which belongs to the sibling enrollment knowledge base
compensation schedules, which belong to the sibling renewal knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a federal plan-year rule release, a state department-of-insurance bulletin, or a carrier marketing-policy revision changes what a named obligation class requires

pros.claim: Resolving each activity to a named governing layer converts diffuse compliance anxiety into a small set of checkable obligations an agent can actually satisfy
pros.example: an agent invited to leave flyers at a pharmacy counter resolves it in minutes to the material-review path plus the nominal-gift and unsolicited-contact classes instead of guessing

pros.claim: A dated map makes disagreement productive because it forces the question of which layer and which year a claimed rule comes from
pros.example: an upline trainer asserts a contact window; the map shows the assertion has no locator, so the agent checks the current-year source before acting

cons.claim: The map is a snapshot that decays every plan year and breeds false confidence when the verification dates are ignored
cons.example: an agent quoting a remembered prior-year contact rule to justify an outreach campaign that this year's rules no longer permit

cons.claim: Building it costs real hours before a single prospect is contacted, which is hard to justify to an agent under revenue pressure
cons.example: a new agent spending the week before certification season reading carrier marketing policies instead of buying leads

failure_modes: treating an upline's verbal guidance as the rule text and never locating the source
assuming one state's producer-conduct rule applies in a neighbouring state where the agent also holds a non-resident licence
reading a permissive carrier policy as if it relaxed a stricter federal or state obligation
letting the map's verification dates go stale so the whole structure silently describes a prior plan year
acceptance_tests: every obligation class in the map names its governing layer, a locator for the current-year text, and the date that text was last read
at least one activity class shows a documented instance where the strictest of two conflicting layers was applied
revisit_triggers: a new plan-year rule set or carrier marketing policy is published
the agent adds a state, a carrier, or an upline relationship
a carrier or regulator issues a bulletin, a clarification, or an enforcement action affecting agent conduct

nodes.definition: Install, as a standing operating rule rather than a stated value, the principle that when a growth tactic and a compliance obligation collide the obligation wins and the tactic is redesigned or abandoned. Making it real means building the small gate that catches the profitable-but-unprovable idea before it runs: every prospecting, marketing, or partnership idea is written down in one paragraph with the rule class it touches, the permission or approval artifact that will exist after it runs, and a named approver who signed off; ideas that cannot produce an artifact do not run. The characteristic tests are unglamorous - the ride-along at a friendly clinic, the just-this-once call to a lead whose permission has expired, the flyer that skipped review because the print shop had a deadline - and the rule's real content is the escalation path when no compliant version exists: the tactic is dropped outright and the resulting gap is filled from already-approved sources instead of being rationalized.

included: the written pre-approval gate for any new tactic
the artifact-must-exist test
the abandon-and-substitute escalation path when no compliant version exists
excluded: judging the commercial merit or expected yield of a tactic
retention and service tactics aimed at existing clients, which belong to the sibling renewal knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an enforcement action, carrier bulletin, or internal finding shows a tactic class the gate currently passes is no longer defensible

pros.claim: A pre-run written gate stops the single-decision catastrophes that end practices, because the tempting shortcuts are exactly the ones that cannot describe their own evidence trail
pros.example: an idea to hand a stack of business cards to a hospital discharge planner fails the gate on the first line because no permission artifact can exist for the resulting calls

pros.claim: Deciding the rule in advance removes the decision from the moment of temptation, when a quota deadline makes every rationalization sound reasonable
pros.example: an agent short of a season goal in the last week reaches for an expired-permission list and the standing rule refuses it without needing a fresh argument

cons.claim: The gate genuinely costs volume, and a competitor willing to ignore it will out-produce a compliant agent in the short run
cons.example: watching a local competitor run unsolicited door knocking through a whole season and write more business before the complaints catch up

cons.claim: A gate applied mechanically can also kill benign activity and train the agent to route everything through slow approval
cons.example: delaying a purely educational library talk for weeks because the checklist was written as if every activity were plan-specific marketing

failure_modes: treating the principle as a slogan with no written gate behind it
granting a self-approval exception during the busiest weeks, when the risk is highest
allowing an upline's enthusiasm to substitute for the named approver and the artifact test
abandoning a tactic without substituting an approved source, so the revenue gap drives the next shortcut
acceptance_tests: every tactic run in the current plan year has a one-paragraph pre-approval record naming its rule class, its resulting artifact, and its approver
at least one tactic in the log is recorded as abandoned with the approved substitute that filled the gap
revisit_triggers: a tactic is proposed that the existing checklist cannot classify
a complaint or audit finding traces back to a tactic that passed the gate
a rule change makes a previously approved tactic non-compliant

nodes.definition: Treat the Medicare-eligible population as a protected class and build the contact and conversation habits that duty implies, because a meaningful share of prospects are older, recently bereaved, hard of hearing, limited in English, cognitively impaired, or dependent on a caregiver who may or may not hold legal authority. Operationally this means slowing the pace and repeating the material points, offering to include a family member or authorized representative and documenting the offer, establishing who actually holds authority to sign before any form appears, checking comprehension by asking the beneficiary to restate in their own words what they are choosing and why, and stopping the interaction outright when capacity is genuinely in doubt rather than proceeding to a signature that a family member will later contest. The duty also carries affirmative bans that override every sales instinct: no manufactured urgency, no fear framing about losing coverage or benefits, no ambiguity about who is calling and whom the agent represents, and no continuing after a request to stop.

included: pacing, repetition, and comprehension confirmation habits
authority and representative verification before any signature
the hard-stop rule when capacity is in doubt
the banned pressure, urgency, and fear tactics
excluded: clinical assessment of cognitive capacity, which no agent is licensed to perform
the plan-fit discussion itself, which belongs to the sibling enrollment knowledge base
guardianship or power-of-attorney legal advice, which belongs to counsel

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a complaint, a family dispute, or a revised senior-protection rule shows the current pacing, authority, or comprehension habits are insufficient

pros.claim: Comprehension checks and documented accommodations prevent the single most damaging complaint class, the enrollment a beneficiary or family says was never understood
pros.example: asking a prospect to describe in their own words what changes for their pharmacy and hearing a wrong answer, which stops the appointment before a signature exists

pros.claim: A pre-decided hard-stop rule protects the agent from the pressure a family member or the beneficiary themselves can apply in the moment
pros.example: a prospect who cannot recall the conversation from ten minutes earlier insists on signing today, and the standing rule ends the meeting with a follow-up scheduled with a relative present

cons.claim: Slower, accommodation-heavy appointments materially reduce the number of households an agent can serve in a peak season
cons.example: a single appointment stretching across two visits because a daughter can only attend on a weekend during the busiest weeks of the year

cons.claim: Capacity judgements by an unqualified observer can be wrong in both directions and may read as patronizing to a fully capable prospect
cons.example: treating a hard-of-hearing but entirely sharp retired engineer as impaired and losing their trust in the first ten minutes

failure_modes: accepting an adult child's instruction to enroll a parent who is not present and has granted no documented authority
using loss-of-coverage fear or an invented deadline to move a hesitant prospect
mistaking politeness and nodding for comprehension and never asking the beneficiary to restate the choice
failing to record that an accommodation or a representative was offered, so a later dispute has no evidence either way
acceptance_tests: every file records who was present, what accommodation was offered, and the beneficiary's own restatement of what they were choosing
at least one documented instance exists in the practice where an interaction was stopped or deferred on capacity or authority grounds
revisit_triggers: a family member disputes an interaction or an enrollment
a state or federal rule on senior-consumer protection or unfair conduct is revised
the practice begins serving a population with new language or accessibility needs

nodes.definition: Hold the line, in every outreach setting, between explaining how Medicare-related coverage works and telling a particular person which plan to take. In talks, written material, social content, and first conversations the agent teaches mechanisms - how the coverage parts relate, what a network is, what a formulary is, what an enrollment period is, what a supplement does that an all-in-one plan does not - and routes every request for a personal answer into a structured needs conversation the beneficiary drives and decides. This node governs the marketing-side half of that line: what may be claimed in a public setting, how to answer an individual's question in front of a room without turning it into a personal recommendation for everyone listening, and the standing disclosure that the agent represents specific contracted carriers rather than the government, Medicare, or every plan available in the county. The enrollment-conversation half of the line, including how the needs discussion itself is run, belongs to the sibling enrollment knowledge base.

included: mechanism-level education in public and outreach settings
handling an individual question in a group without giving a public recommendation
the standing who-I-represent and not-the-government disclosure
excluded: the structured needs-and-fit conversation and its artifacts, which belong to the sibling enrollment knowledge base
medical, legal, or tax opinions of any kind
telling a beneficiary which plan is best for them

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a revised disclosure or marketing-communication rule changes what may be said in a public educational setting

pros.claim: Teaching mechanisms rather than recommending plans builds durable trust and produces prospects who arrive already able to participate in their own decision
pros.example: a library talk that explains what a formulary tier is, after which attendees bring their actual medication lists to appointments instead of arriving blank

pros.claim: The line protects the agent from the most common informal violation, the confident public answer to a private situation
pros.example: redirecting a question about a specific cancer drug from the microphone to a private appointment where the person's own drug list can be checked

cons.claim: Mechanism-level education frustrates prospects who came wanting a direct answer and may feel evasive
cons.example: an attendee who asks which plan is best and hears a description of trade-offs instead, then leaves for an agent who will simply tell them

cons.claim: Education-first outreach converts slowly and its return is hard to attribute, which makes it the first activity cut under pressure
cons.example: a monthly senior-center class that produces appointments months later, credited to word of mouth rather than to the class

failure_modes: answering a specific person's specific situation from the front of a room
implying government affiliation or endorsement by using official-looking imagery or language in educational material
claiming or implying that the agent can offer every plan available rather than the carriers actually contracted
letting an educational session drift into plan-specific promotion once questions start
acceptance_tests: every public-facing talk or piece contains the who-I-represent and not-the-government disclosure in the form the current rules require
the standing redirect script for individual questions asked in public is written down and used
revisit_triggers: a disclosure requirement or its required wording class changes for the plan year
attendee questions repeatedly push a session past the education line
the carrier portfolio changes, altering what the agent may truthfully say they represent

nodes.definition: Maintain the state producer licence class - resident and, for every other state the book touches, non-resident - as the base permission to transact anything at all: pre-licensing and examination in the health line and, where the book needs it, the life line, the state appointment or filing where the state requires one, continuing-education obligations on a renewal cycle, mandatory notification of address and name changes, and disclosure of any adverse administrative or criminal action. The expert work here is calendar work rather than knowledge work: every renewal, continuing-education deadline, and non-resident maintenance date across the whole footprint sits in one calendar with lead time long enough that a lapse cannot happen, and status is confirmed through the state's own public lookup rather than from a spreadsheet or an upline's roster. Specific hours, renewal periods, reciprocity treatment, and reinstatement paths differ by state and change; verify current requirements with each state's insurance department before relying on any of them.

included: resident and non-resident licence classes and their renewal calendar
continuing-education obligation tracking
state lookup verification and adverse-action disclosure duties
excluded: carrier appointment and product certification, which are separate downstream credentials
any assertion of specific hour counts, fees, or renewal intervals, which are state-specific and must be verified

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a state insurance department revises licensing, continuing-education, appointment, or reinstatement requirements for producers

pros.claim: A single footprint-wide calendar with long lead time makes the most avoidable business-ending event, a silent lapse, structurally impossible
pros.example: a non-resident licence in a neighbouring state renewing on a different month than the resident licence, caught by the calendar rather than by a declined application

pros.claim: Verifying through the state's own lookup catches administrative problems the agent never received mail about
pros.example: discovering an address-of-record mismatch that was silently bouncing the state's renewal notices

cons.claim: Multi-state licensing multiplies fixed cost and continuing-education burden well before it multiplies revenue
cons.example: carrying two non-resident licences for a handful of border-town clients whose combined business does not cover the maintenance

cons.claim: Continuing education is easy to satisfy nominally while learning nothing, which creates a false sense of currency
cons.example: clearing a renewal cycle with unrelated coursework while the year's marketing-rule changes go unread

failure_modes: discovering a lapse only when a carrier declines an application or a commission is withheld
letting the state's address of record go stale so renewal notices never arrive
assuming reciprocity means a non-resident licence needs no separate maintenance
failing to disclose an adverse action within the window the state requires
acceptance_tests: every state in the footprint appears in one calendar with its renewal and continuing-education dates and a lead-time reminder
licence status for each state has been confirmed from that state's own lookup within the current cycle and the confirmation is stored
revisit_triggers: the agent adds or drops a state, or a client moves across a state line
a state revises its continuing-education or renewal requirements
any adverse action, name change, or address change occurs

nodes.definition: Run certification season as a dated project with a hard deadline rather than as a chore done when convenient, because until it is finished the agent has no authority to sell anything for the coming plan year. The stack has two layers: an industry-standard annual Medicare and fraud-waste-abuse training course, commonly the AHIP-class course that most carriers accept as a prerequisite, followed by each contracted carrier's own product and compliance modules. The sequencing judgement is what separates a smooth season from a lost one - complete the shared annual training first because carriers gate their modules on it, then take carrier modules in the order the book's revenue actually depends on them, so that if something goes wrong the loss lands on the least important carrier. Attempt limits, retake waiting periods, submission deadlines, and which shared course a given carrier will accept vary by carrier and by plan year and must be read from each carrier's own portal each cycle; store the completion evidence per carrier per year rather than trusting the portal to remember.

included: the shared annual training class and its prerequisite role
per-carrier product and compliance module sequencing
attempt-limit, deadline, and evidence-retention discipline
excluded: the state licence and continuing education that precede it
the carrier's composite ready-to-sell finding, which is verified separately
plan benefit knowledge for the enrollment conversation, which belongs to the sibling enrollment knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier publishes new certification requirements, accepted-course rules, attempt limits, or deadlines for the coming plan year

pros.claim: Sequencing by revenue dependence contains the damage when a module goes wrong, because the exposure lands where the book is thinnest
pros.example: an agent hitting an attempt limit on the fourth carrier's module rather than on the carrier that writes most of the book

pros.claim: Finishing early converts certification from a risk into an advantage, since the calendar frees up exactly when competitors are still testing
pros.example: having ready-to-sell status confirmed before the season's marketing window opens while others are still retaking modules

cons.claim: The cycle repeats in full every year regardless of how long the agent has practised, consuming a block of prime preparation time
cons.example: spending the weeks before a season on modules that largely restate the prior year's content

cons.claim: Carrying many carrier contracts makes the certification load a real constraint on portfolio breadth
cons.example: an agent contracted with eight carriers who cannot finish all product modules before the season and must sit out two of them

failure_modes: starting carrier modules before the shared annual training that gates them
exhausting attempt limits on a rushed module and triggering a waiting period that spans the deadline
relying on a carrier portal to retain proof of completion instead of storing the evidence independently
assuming a carrier accepts the same shared course it accepted last year
acceptance_tests: a per-carrier certification tracker shows the completion date, the accepted course, and stored evidence for the current plan year
the shared annual training is recorded as completed before any carrier product module was attempted
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes its accepted training, its attempt limits, or its deadline
a new carrier contract is added mid-cycle
a module is failed or a waiting period is triggered

nodes.definition: Assemble and maintain the carrier contract stack that turns a licensed, certified agent into someone a specific carrier will actually pay: the application and background or vetting package, evidence of licence and errors-and-omissions coverage, banking and tax registration, and the resulting appointment and writing number per carrier, per state, and per product line. Two kinds of expert judgement live here. The first is portfolio design - contract deeply enough to serve the plan landscape the agent's counties actually contain, without carrying so many carriers that certification season becomes unfinishable or that thin relationships attract no support. The second is reading the contract terms that only bite later: how the carrier defines the writing agent of record, its charge-back and termination-for-cause language, its marketing-material and social-media policy, its data-handling terms, and what it obliges the agent to self-report. Errors-and-omissions coverage class, limits, retroactive dates, and whether an upline's group policy actually covers the agent's own activity are contract-specific facts to confirm in writing rather than assume.

included: the contracting and appointment package and its per-state, per-product structure
carrier portfolio breadth judgement
the contract terms that govern conduct, charge-backs, and self-reporting
errors-and-omissions coverage class verification
excluded: upline hierarchy choice and release policy, which is treated as its own unit
commission rates and renewal schedules, which are regulated mechanisms covered in the sibling renewal knowledge base
product and benefit knowledge, which belongs to the sibling enrollment knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier amends its producer agreement, marketing policy, or appointment requirements, or the local plan landscape shifts enough to change which carriers are needed

pros.claim: A carrier portfolio matched to the actual local plan landscape lets a needs-driven comparison be honest, because the agent is not forced to present only what they happen to hold
pros.example: carrying the carriers whose networks include the two hospital systems most local beneficiaries actually use

pros.claim: Reading the charge-back, agent-of-record, and self-reporting terms before signing prevents the disputes that surface only after a season of production
pros.example: learning at contracting time, not afterwards, how the carrier treats a rapid disenrollment for compensation purposes

cons.claim: Every added carrier multiplies annual certification load, portal maintenance, and material-review paths for the same twenty-four hours
cons.example: an eighth carrier contract that produces a handful of enrollments while adding a full module set and another marketing policy to track

cons.claim: Contract terms are offered on a take-it-or-leave-it basis, so diligence informs the decision but rarely changes the terms
cons.example: reading an unfavourable termination clause and having no realistic option except to accept it or forgo the carrier

failure_modes: signing without reading the marketing-policy and self-reporting clauses that govern daily conduct
assuming an upline group errors-and-omissions policy covers the agent's independent activity
contracting for a state or product line the agent is not licensed or certified to sell
collecting carriers for breadth while leaving several with too little production to sustain support
acceptance_tests: a contract register lists each carrier with its states, product lines, writing number, and the date the executed contract and errors-and-omissions evidence were stored
for every carrier in the register the charge-back, agent-of-record, marketing-policy, and self-reporting clauses have been read and summarized in the agent's own words
revisit_triggers: a carrier issues a contract amendment or a revised marketing policy
the local plan landscape changes so the current carrier set no longer covers the needs the agent sees
errors-and-omissions coverage renews, changes carriers, or changes retroactive date

nodes.definition: Understand the upline structure - the field-marketing or independent-marketing organization hierarchy a contract is written through, the assignment of compensation and overrides along it, and the release mechanism - as the machinery that decides how easily the agent can ever change their mind. A carrier contract written through a hierarchy typically routes compensation, support, and often certification and material-review assistance through that upline; moving that contract to a different upline generally requires either a written release from the current one or the expiry of a carrier-defined dormancy period whose length and conditions are set by the carrier's own policy rather than negotiated. The work is therefore diligence before signing, not after: obtain the release policy in writing, establish exactly which services the override actually buys, avoid the common trap of contracting with the same carrier twice through different uplines, and treat compensation and override levels as regulated and contract-set mechanisms to verify in the current schedule rather than as promised numbers.

included: hierarchy structure and how compensation assignment flows through it
release and dormancy mechanics as a mobility constraint
diligence on what upline services the override actually purchases
excluded: stating any specific commission, override, or bonus figure, which is schedule- and contract-set and must be verified
renewal compensation mechanics over the life of a book, which belong to the sibling renewal knowledge base
recruiting or building a downline hierarchy as a separate business model

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier or upline publishes revised release, dormancy, or hierarchy-assignment policy, or the agent's experience shows the override services are not being delivered

pros.claim: Getting the release policy in writing before signing preserves the option to change uplines later, which is the single most expensive option agents give away unknowingly
pros.example: an agent who confirms the release terms in advance and can move a carrier contract when the upline's promised support never materializes

pros.claim: Naming the services an override buys makes the relationship evaluable instead of sentimental
pros.example: listing certification help, material review turnaround, and lead programs as the deliverables, then noticing at renewal that only one is actually provided

cons.claim: Hierarchy diligence is asked for at exactly the moment an agent has the least leverage and the most urgency to get contracted before a season
cons.example: a new agent needing ready-to-sell status in weeks and signing whatever hierarchy paperwork arrives first

cons.claim: Optimizing for mobility can cost real support, because the uplines most willing to release are not always the ones investing most in their agents
cons.example: choosing a hands-off aggregator for its easy release policy and then having no help when a carrier portal problem blocks certification

failure_modes: signing hierarchy paperwork without ever seeing the carrier's release and dormancy policy
contracting with the same carrier through two different uplines and creating a conflict the carrier resolves against the agent
believing a verbal promise about compensation level rather than the contract schedule
discovering only at a moment of dispute that the support the override paid for was never contractual
acceptance_tests: for every carrier contract the upline and the carrier release or dormancy policy are recorded in writing before submission
the services expected from each upline are listed and reviewed against what was actually delivered at least once per plan year
revisit_triggers: an upline changes ownership, services, or compensation assignment
a carrier revises its release or dormancy policy
the agent considers adding a carrier already held through another hierarchy

nodes.definition: Collapse the whole credential stack into one per-carrier, per-state, per-product ready-to-sell matrix and re-verify it from each carrier's own portal before any marketing or enrollment activity touches that carrier, because ready-to-sell is not the agent's conclusion but the carrier's composite finding - licence active, appointment in force, current-year certification passed, contract in good standing - and it can turn false without notice when any single input lapses. The operating habits are a full pre-season sweep that produces a stored export or screenshot per carrier, and a same-day re-check before an appointment for a product the agent has not written recently or in a state they rarely serve. This node is deliberately a gate rather than a reference: activity conducted while not ready to sell is the failure that most reliably voids compensation, invalidates an enrollment for the beneficiary, and triggers carrier action, and it is entirely preventable by a check that takes minutes.

included: the composite per-carrier, per-state, per-product status matrix
pre-season sweep and same-day pre-appointment re-check
stored portal evidence of status at the time of activity
excluded: the underlying licence, certification, and contracting work that feeds the status
any enrollment-period or plan-selection decision, which belongs to the sibling enrollment knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier changes how it computes or displays selling authority, or a status flip is discovered that the current sweep cadence would have missed

pros.claim: One composite matrix removes the whole class of accidental unauthorized activity, because the agent never has to reason from four separate systems under time pressure
pros.example: a same-day check catching that a carrier flipped status after an appointment-in-a-new-state filing lapsed, before the appointment rather than after the application

pros.claim: Stored evidence of status at the time of activity is the cleanest possible answer to a later carrier question
pros.example: producing the dated portal export showing ready-to-sell status on the day an application was written

cons.claim: Portals disagree, lag, and occasionally show stale status, so the matrix can be wrong in both directions and still look authoritative
cons.example: a carrier portal continuing to display ready-to-sell for a state whose appointment filing has actually been terminated

cons.claim: Re-verification across many carriers is repetitive manual work that invites shortcuts exactly when the season is busiest
cons.example: skipping the same-day check during the peak weeks because the pre-season sweep was clean

failure_modes: treating the pre-season sweep as valid for the whole season while inputs quietly lapse
relying on an upline's roster or a spreadsheet rather than the carrier's own portal
checking only the carrier and forgetting the state or product dimension of the status
writing an application in a state where the appointment was never filed
acceptance_tests: a stored, dated status export exists per carrier, state, and product line for the current plan year
no application in the current plan year lacks evidence of ready-to-sell status on or before its written date
revisit_triggers: any certification, licence, appointment, or contract input changes
a carrier portal shows a status change or the agent adds a state or product
an appointment is scheduled for a carrier or state not written recently

nodes.definition: Establish, scope, and time-bound a beneficiary's permission before initiating contact, and treat the several permission regimes as separate requirements that stack rather than as one loose idea of consent: the Medicare marketing rule class governing unsolicited contact about plans, the telephone-consumer class governing calls and texts including do-not-call scrubbing and the prior-express-written-consent standard for automated outreach, and each carrier's own documentation standard for what it will accept as proof. The expert work is knowing precisely what a given permission covers - which product types, which channels, for how long, obtained by whom - and re-obtaining it rather than stretching it, together with the discipline that a beneficiary who asked about one product class has not thereby invited a call about another, and that an inbound request answers only the question it asked. Permitted channels, expiry windows, and what counts as an inbound request are set by current rules that differ across the regimes and change between plan years; verify the current-year text before relying on any specific window.

included: the stacked consent regimes and what each governs
scope, channel, and expiry discipline for a given permission
do-not-call and internal suppression hygiene
excluded: the record system that stores the artifacts, which is treated as its own unit
the pre-appointment product-scope agreement, which is a distinct artifact
what is discussed inside an enrollment conversation, which belongs to the sibling enrollment knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any of the stacked consent regimes revises permitted channels, expiry, or proof standards, or a carrier tightens what artifact it will accept

pros.claim: Scoping permission explicitly by product, channel, and window turns the most common grey-area argument into a lookup
pros.example: a prospect who requested drug-coverage information online is not called about a different product class because the stored scope says otherwise

pros.claim: Honouring expiry rather than stretching it prevents the complaint pattern that regulators and carriers find most damning, contact the consumer does not remember inviting
pros.example: declining to work a months-old inbound web form and instead re-inviting contact through a compliant channel

cons.claim: Strict scoping strands genuinely interested prospects whose permission has lapsed on a technicality
cons.example: a prospect who asked for information before a birthday, went quiet, and can no longer be called when they become eligible

cons.claim: Multiple stacking regimes make the permitted action genuinely hard to determine, and the strictest reading can be more restrictive than any single rule requires
cons.example: a text message that one regime would permit and another would not, resolved conservatively at the cost of a responsive answer

failure_modes: treating any inbound contact as open-ended permission for all products and channels
reusing a permission obtained for one household member to contact a spouse or relative
skipping do-not-call and internal suppression checks on a purchased list
letting a verbal permission exist only in memory with no artifact attached to the outreach it authorized
acceptance_tests: every outbound contact traces to a stored permission artifact naming the product types, the channel, the source, and the date
suppression and do-not-call checks are recorded before any campaign against a list
revisit_triggers: a plan-year change to the marketing or telephone-consent rule classes
a carrier revises what it accepts as proof of permission
a new outreach channel such as messaging or automated dialing is introduced

nodes.definition: Capture the beneficiary's documented agreement about which product types will be discussed before a personal marketing appointment begins, hold the discussion inside that scope, and re-paper the scope before adding a product type rather than afterwards. The unit covers the form's required elements - the beneficiary's agreement, the product types named, the date, agent identification, and the statement that no obligation to enroll arises - the timing class, since current rules impose a required interval between the documented agreement and the appointment with narrowly defined exceptions, the permitted capture methods, and the retention obligation that makes the form useful later. The hard parts are the ordinary awkward moments rather than the form itself: the beneficiary who asks mid-appointment about a product outside the scope, the walk-in who wants to talk today, the appointment that reschedules across a plan-year boundary, and the referral who joins a spouse's meeting. Timing intervals, exceptions, acceptable formats, and retention periods are set by current rules and carrier policy and must be verified for the current plan year.

included: required elements of the scope agreement and its timing class
in-appointment scope discipline and re-papering
capture methods and retention obligations
excluded: the needs-and-fit conversation and plan comparison held inside the appointment, which belong to the sibling enrollment knowledge base
general permission to contact, which is a separate and earlier artifact

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: current-year rules or carrier policy change the required interval, elements, exceptions, or retention treatment of the scope agreement

pros.claim: A scope agreed in advance makes the appointment calmer and narrower, which protects both the beneficiary and the agent from a sprawling cross-sell
pros.example: an appointment that stays on health coverage rather than drifting into an unrelated product the beneficiary never agreed to hear about

pros.claim: The stored form is the cheapest possible defence against a later claim about what was discussed
pros.example: producing the dated agreement showing the beneficiary named the product types before the visit

cons.claim: The timing interval genuinely costs appointments, because a prospect ready to talk today may not be reachable tomorrow
cons.example: a walk-in at a community event who wants to meet immediately and must instead be scheduled after the required interval unless a narrow exception applies

cons.claim: Re-papering mid-appointment interrupts the conversation at the worst moment and can read as bureaucratic to the beneficiary
cons.example: stopping to document a new scope when a prospect raises a second product type in the middle of a productive discussion

failure_modes: backdating or completing the form after the appointment to satisfy the interval
discussing a product type the scope does not cover because the beneficiary raised it first
letting a scope captured for one plan year carry into an appointment that slipped past the boundary
capturing the form in a way the carrier will not accept as valid proof
acceptance_tests: every personal marketing appointment file contains a scope agreement dated before the appointment with all required elements present
any product type discussed beyond the original scope has its own re-papered agreement in the same file
revisit_triggers: the timing interval, exception set, or accepted formats change for the plan year
a carrier rejects a captured form as insufficient
the practice adopts a new capture method such as electronic or recorded agreement

nodes.definition: Maintain a written catalog that separates practices which are flatly prohibited from those permitted only with conditions attached, and rehearse it until it governs behaviour under pressure rather than being consulted afterwards. The prohibited classes include unsolicited door-to-door and other unsolicited direct contact about plans, providing or offering meals at sales events, using absolute superlatives or implying government or Medicare endorsement of the agent, misusing the Medicare name or plan logos, collecting or accepting enrollment applications at an event advertised as educational, cross-selling a non-health product class inside a Medicare appointment without a separate agreed scope, offering anything above the nominal-value gift class or conditioning any gift on enrolling, targeting or steering by health status, and claiming to represent every plan available. The conditional classes - permitted promotional items, permitted event conduct, permitted comparative statements - are safe only with their conditions attached, so the catalog stores each condition beside its practice. Specific value thresholds and permitted-conduct definitions are set by current-year rules and must be verified rather than remembered.

included: the absolute prohibition list as behaviour rules
the conditional-permission list with each condition stored beside its practice
the rehearsal habit that makes the catalog operative in real time
excluded: enrollment-period and plan-comparison conduct inside the enrollment conversation, which belongs to the sibling enrollment knowledge base
asserting any specific dollar threshold as fact, which must be verified in current-year rules

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a plan-year rule release, carrier bulletin, or enforcement action changes what is prohibited or alters the condition attached to a permitted practice

pros.claim: Splitting absolute from conditional prohibitions stops the two opposite errors, doing a banned thing and refusing a permitted one
pros.example: an agent who correctly declines to provide a meal at a sales event but still offers a permitted low-value promotional item without conditioning it on enrollment

pros.claim: A rehearsed catalog survives the moment of pressure, which is the only moment that matters
pros.example: answering a prospect's request for the best plan available with a compliant comparison instead of a superlative, without pausing to think

cons.claim: A catalog written once decays quietly as thresholds and definitions change between plan years
cons.example: an agent applying a remembered gift-value limit that the current-year rules have since revised

cons.claim: Rules stated as a list encourage literal compliance without the judgement that catches novel variants of the same abuse
cons.example: an outreach idea that avoids every listed prohibition while still amounting to unsolicited contact by another route

failure_modes: casual superlatives in conversation that a monitored call captures verbatim
accepting an application handed over at an educational event rather than scheduling a separate compliant appointment
letting a gift or refreshment become an inducement by tying it to enrolling
implying government affiliation through official-looking imagery, envelope design, or scripted language
acceptance_tests: the catalog exists in writing with each conditional practice stored next to its current-year condition and verification date
a sampled review of recent calls or appointments shows no instance of a listed prohibited practice
revisit_triggers: a plan-year rule release changes a threshold, a definition, or the prohibition list itself
a monitored call, secret shop, or complaint surfaces a practice the catalog does not cover
a new marketing channel or partnership creates a variant the catalog has not classified

nodes.definition: Route every externally facing piece through a review path before it exists in public, starting from the classification question that determines everything else: does the piece market specific plans, in which case filing, carrier approval, and disclosure obligations generally attach, or is it general communication material that does not. From there the work is procedural and unglamorous - submit plan-specific pieces to the carrier's material-review process allowing for its stated turnaround rather than the day before printing, apply the required disclosure classes including the third-party marketing disclaimer, the not-connected-with-or-endorsed-by-the-government statement, and an honest statement of how many carriers and plans the agent actually represents, and version every approved piece to a plan year so last season's flyer cannot walk back into a rack. The highest-leverage habit is building a small library of approved templates that are cleared once and reused, because violations are overwhelmingly born in one-off pieces made under deadline.

included: the plan-specific versus general communication classification
carrier submission and approval turnaround planning
required disclosure classes and plan-year versioning
an approved reusable template library
excluded: online-specific problems of durability, targeting, and public comment, which are treated as their own unit
plan benefit content accuracy, which belongs to the sibling enrollment knowledge base
asserting a specific turnaround time or filing deadline as fact

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier or rule change alters material classification, required disclosures, or the review path and its turnaround

pros.claim: An approved template library converts the riskiest recurring activity into a low-effort one and removes deadline pressure as a cause of violations
pros.example: producing an event flyer for a new date from a cleared template instead of designing a fresh piece the week before

pros.claim: Plan-year versioning makes the annual purge mechanical rather than archaeological
pros.example: every printed piece carrying a plan-year marker so the pre-season sweep can pull the outdated ones by sight

cons.claim: Review turnaround is outside the agent's control and can miss a market window entirely
cons.example: a seasonal piece submitted with what seemed like ample lead time returning with required changes after the window closed

cons.claim: Template reuse produces sameness that weakens differentiation in a crowded local market
cons.example: several local agents from the same upline circulating visibly identical approved flyers

failure_modes: misclassifying a plan-specific piece as general communication to avoid the review path
publishing before approval returns because a print or event deadline moved
omitting a required disclosure class from a piece that otherwise passed review
leaving prior-year approved material in circulation after the plan-year boundary
acceptance_tests: every public piece carries its classification, its approval identifier where required, its disclosure block, and its plan-year marker
an inventory of circulating material exists and shows no prior-year piece still in use
revisit_triggers: a disclosure requirement or its wording class changes for the plan year
a carrier changes its material-review process or turnaround
the agent's represented carrier count changes, invalidating the representation statement

nodes.definition: Run the two event classes as genuinely different products rather than as one event with different labels. An educational event is advertised as educational, teaches how coverage works, excludes plan-specific sales activity and application collection, and exists to build presence and trust; a marketing or sales event does present specific plans and may take enrollments, under its own conduct, advertising, and reporting rules. The operational envelope around both is where the work actually is: reporting or registering the event with the carrier within its required lead time and reporting cancellations, advertising it truthfully in reviewed material that matches the event class, keeping sign-in sheets and any permission capture voluntary and clearly labelled as optional, running the room so that an individual question does not become a public personal recommendation, honouring the meal prohibition and the nominal-gift class, and leaving with a record of what was presented and to whom. Event definitions, reporting lead times, cancellation duties, and conduct rules are set by current rules and carrier policy and must be verified each plan year.

included: the two event classes and what separates them in practice
carrier reporting, advertising, and cancellation duties
in-room conduct, sign-in, and gift discipline
excluded: the ongoing community partnership strategy that supplies venues and audiences, which is treated as its own unit
the enrollment conversation that follows an event, which belongs to the sibling enrollment knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: current-year rules or carrier policy revise the event class definitions, reporting duties, or permitted in-room conduct

pros.claim: Keeping the classes separate lets the educational event do the trust work that no sales event can, while the sales event does the transaction work honestly
pros.example: a library class that never mentions a plan name, followed weeks later by separately advertised plan-specific sessions attended by the same people

pros.claim: Reporting and truthful advertising make the event defensible on the day a carrier reviews it
pros.example: producing the reported event record, the approved advertisement, and the optional-labelled sign-in sheet for a monitored session

cons.claim: Events are expensive in time and cash with attendance that is genuinely unpredictable
cons.example: a booked room, printed materials, and an afternoon spent for a handful of attendees during a busy week

cons.claim: The educational class forbids exactly what attendees most want, which makes the session feel incomplete to the audience
cons.example: an attendee who came to hear which local plans exist and leaves with mechanisms rather than names

failure_modes: letting an educational event drift into plan-specific promotion once the questions start
accepting an application or a signed form at an event advertised as educational
missing the carrier reporting lead time or failing to report a cancellation
making sign-in feel mandatory or capturing permission without explaining it is optional
acceptance_tests: every event has a stored record of its class, its carrier reporting confirmation, its approved advertisement, and its optional-labelled sign-in
no educational event record shows an application, a signed enrollment form, or plan-specific promotional material
revisit_triggers: event definitions, reporting lead times, or conduct rules change for the plan year
a carrier or monitor observes an event and issues a finding
a venue partner changes what it will allow on its premises

nodes.definition: Treat third-party lead generation as an inherited-liability decision rather than a purchasing decision. Where the agent buys from, or themselves acts as, an entity in the third-party marketing organization class, the current rule set attaches obligations that travel with the lead: a disclaimer class stating how many plans and carriers are actually represented, restrictions on how consumer information may be collected, shared, and re-sold, and a recording and retention obligation class covering sales and enrollment calls. Carriers hold the agent responsible for what the vendor did to produce the lead, so the work is diligence before the first purchase - obtain the actual consent language and a copy of the capture page rather than a summary, establish whether the lead was represented as exclusive or shared and how many times it has been sold, confirm the vendor's script and disclaimer would survive review, and retain the consent artifact alongside the lead record instead of trusting the vendor to hold it. Disclaimer wording, recording scope, and retention periods are set by current-year rules and must be verified.

included: vendor diligence on consent provenance and capture pages
the disclaimer, recording, and retention obligation classes attached to third-party lead activity
exclusivity and resale verification
excluded: channel-mix and diversification strategy, which is treated as its own unit
the enrollment call content itself, which belongs to the sibling enrollment knowledge base
stating any specific lead price or conversion rate as fact

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a rule change alters third-party marketing obligations, or a vendor audit reveals consent provenance that does not match what was represented

pros.claim: Obtaining the actual capture page and consent language converts an unverifiable purchase into an auditable one
pros.example: rejecting a batch whose capture page offered a government benefits review rather than contact from an insurance agent

pros.claim: Purchased leads can genuinely fill a calendar quickly when the provenance is clean, which no other channel does on demand
pros.example: a vetted vendor supplying appointment-ready inbound requests during a slow stretch when community channels are dormant

cons.claim: The agent carries the compliance exposure for conduct they did not perform and cannot fully observe
cons.example: a complaint about a misleading advertisement the vendor ran, arriving at the agent because the agent made the call

cons.claim: Shared leads produce contact fatigue that harms the beneficiary and the agent's reputation at once
cons.example: a beneficiary who receives several calls the same afternoon from agents who bought the same record

failure_modes: accepting a vendor's assurance about consent instead of the artifact itself
failing to apply the required disclaimer at the start of a call the rules require it on
not recording or not retaining calls the applicable rules require to be recorded and kept
buying aged or resold records without checking how many times they have been sold
acceptance_tests: every lead vendor file contains the capture page, the verbatim consent language, the exclusivity representation, and the vendor's compliance attestation
recorded calls exist and are retrievable for the call classes the current rules require to be recorded
revisit_triggers: the disclaimer, recording, or retention obligation class changes
a vendor changes its capture pages, scripts, or resale practice
complaints or quality problems cluster on a single lead source

nodes.definition: Operate the website, social profiles, paid advertising, video, and review presence as marketing material subject to the same classification, review, and disclosure rules as print, while handling three problems that exist only online. Content is durable and dated, so a plan-specific post outlives its plan year and keeps working long after it stopped being accurate; platform targeting tools can construct audiences by inferred health status or other attributes that create discriminatory steering the agent never consciously chose; and public comment threads turn a general post into a request for individual advice in front of an audience. The unit of work is a publishing standard that answers all three: what may be posted without review and what must go through it, the disclosure block that appears on every profile and page, a plan-year purge and re-version pass over dated content, targeting settings that are documented and reviewed rather than left to platform defaults, and a standing rule that individual questions move to a private channel where permission and scope can be captured properly, with an archive of what was published and when.

included: classification and review of online assets
durability, plan-year purge, and publication archive
targeting-setting documentation and the discriminatory-steering risk
moving public individual questions to a private compliant channel
excluded: general material classification and disclosure rules, which are defined in the material-review unit
search and advertising economics, which are business decisions outside the compliance frame
client service conversations, which belong to the sibling renewal knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a platform policy change, a disclosure rule change, or a content audit showing dated plan-specific material still live

pros.claim: A written publishing standard lets an agent maintain a real online presence without a fresh compliance decision on every post
pros.example: a monthly educational explainer published from an approved template while plan-specific claims stay off the feed entirely

pros.claim: Documented targeting settings turn an invisible risk into a reviewable one
pros.example: recording that an advertisement was targeted by geography and age eligibility only, with no health-related interest categories

cons.claim: Online content decays into non-compliance by simply remaining published, so the maintenance burden never ends
cons.example: an old post naming a plan benefit that changed, still ranking in local search two years later

cons.claim: The compliant version of online marketing is duller than what unconstrained competitors publish, which costs reach
cons.example: a competitor's specific benefit claims outperforming an educational post in engagement until the claims draw a complaint

failure_modes: answering a specific person's plan question in a public comment thread
letting platform default targeting build an audience on inferred health attributes
leaving prior-year plan-specific content published after the plan-year boundary
sharing or reposting a carrier or third-party claim that never passed review
acceptance_tests: every profile and page carries the current disclosure block and a plan-year marker where the content is plan-specific
a publication archive exists and the most recent plan-year purge is recorded with the items removed
revisit_triggers: a platform changes its targeting options or advertising policy
a disclosure or material-classification rule changes for the plan year
public comments repeatedly request individual advice

nodes.definition: Design lead generation as a portfolio of compliant sources with genuinely different failure modes rather than as one channel that happens to be working: inbound from a reviewed digital presence, community education presence, referrals from existing clients and professional partners under permitted arrangements, purchased leads from vetted vendors, and carrier-provided programs where they exist. Each source is scored on three axes the agent can actually assess - what compliance exposure it carries, what permission artifact it produces, and whether the practice survives its sudden disappearance - and the mix is then deliberately diversified, because the most common business-interrupting event in this vertical is not a bad month but a single channel vanishing mid-season when a vendor is suspended, a rule changes, a platform policy shifts, or a venue partner ends a relationship. Volumes, costs, and conversion rates are specific to each practice and must be measured from the agent's own book over time rather than assumed from any published figure or upline claim.

included: the compliant source classes and their three-axis scoring
deliberate diversification against single-channel failure
measuring channel performance from the practice's own history
excluded: the specific vendor diligence procedure, which is its own unit
referral cultivation among existing clients as a retention practice, which belongs to the sibling renewal knowledge base
asserting any cost, volume, or conversion figure as a general fact

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the practice's own recorded channel mix, or a source disruption, shows the diversification assumption no longer holds

pros.claim: A mix with uncorrelated failure modes keeps a season alive when any one source stops, which is the difference between a bad quarter and a lost year
pros.example: community and referral flow carrying the calendar through the weeks a suspended vendor supplied nothing

pros.claim: Scoring sources by the artifact they produce, not just by yield, surfaces channels that are cheap in money and expensive in exposure
pros.example: an inexpensive aged-lead source that produces no usable consent artifact and is therefore dropped despite its price

cons.claim: Running several channels at once means none of them is operated well, and the fixed overhead of each is real
cons.example: a monthly class, a content calendar, a referral programme, and a vendor relationship all maintained thinly by one person

cons.claim: Diversification lowers peak efficiency, since concentrating on the best-performing channel would produce more in a stable year
cons.example: sustaining a slow community channel through a season when purchased leads are converting well

failure_modes: building the whole season on one vendor or one platform and discovering the dependency when it stops
adding a channel that cannot produce a permission artifact because its yield looks attractive
judging channels on remembered impressions rather than on the practice's own recorded outcomes
letting the slow, durable channels lapse during peak season so they are cold when they are needed
acceptance_tests: each active source is recorded with its compliance exposure, its permission artifact, and a stated substitution plan if it disappears
no single source accounts for so much of the pipeline that its loss would stop the practice, as shown by the practice's own recorded mix
revisit_triggers: a source is suspended, ends, or changes its terms
the recorded mix drifts toward concentration in one channel
a rule change alters what a channel may do

nodes.definition: Build durable local presence by contributing education repeatedly in the places Medicare-eligible people already are - a standing monthly class at a senior center or library, an educational segment for a pharmacy's patients, a partnership with a local nonprofit or employer preparing retirees - and let permission to contact and referral flow arrive as a byproduct of being useful rather than as the purpose of showing up. The compliance envelope is strict and non-negotiable: the session stays inside the educational class, no applications or enrollment forms are accepted, any promotional item stays inside the nominal-value class and is never conditioned on enrolling, sign-in and permission capture are optional and explained as optional, and any arrangement with a partner organization must not compensate that partner in a way the applicable rules prohibit, which is a written-agreement question to settle with counsel and the carrier rather than an assumption. The payoff is that presence built this way is the least fragile lead source in the practice and the hardest for a competitor or a rule change to take away.

included: repeated educational contribution as a presence strategy
partner-arrangement compliance questions to settle in writing
byproduct permission and referral flow rather than pitch-driven capture
excluded: single-event conduct and reporting mechanics, which are defined in the event-class unit
referral cultivation within an existing book, which belongs to the sibling renewal knowledge base
any compensation arrangement asserted as permissible without verification

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a partner arrangement changes, or rules on partner compensation and event conduct are revised for the plan year

pros.claim: Presence earned by usefulness compounds and cannot be bought away by a better-funded competitor
pros.example: being the person the senior center calls each autumn because the class has run for years

pros.claim: Educational contribution reaches people before they are in a rushed decision, which produces calmer and better-informed appointments
pros.example: attendees arriving months later with their medication lists and questions already organized

cons.claim: The return arrives slowly and is hard to attribute, which makes the channel chronically undervalued and easy to abandon
cons.example: a class run monthly for a year before it produces a steady trickle of appointments credited to word of mouth

cons.claim: Partner relationships create compliance questions that a handshake cannot settle and that counsel time is needed to resolve
cons.example: a pharmacy proposing a referral arrangement that has to be examined before anything is agreed

failure_modes: letting a class drift into plan-specific selling once attendees ask direct questions
conditioning refreshments or a giveaway on attendance turning into enrollment
entering an informal referral arrangement with a partner without written verification that it is permitted
collecting sign-in details in a way that implies attendance requires giving permission to be contacted
acceptance_tests: each recurring venue has a written arrangement stating what the agent does, what the venue provides, and that no prohibited compensation flows in either direction
session records show educational content only, with optional-labelled sign-in and no applications accepted
revisit_triggers: a venue or partner proposes a new arrangement or changes terms
rules affecting partner compensation or event conduct change
attendance or question patterns show the sessions are being treated as sales events

nodes.definition: Operate one record system that holds, per prospect, everything about permission and contact: the permission artifact itself with what was consented to, through which channel, on what date and from which source; do-not-call and internal suppression status with the date it was checked; the scope agreements with their timestamps; and the call recordings that applicable rules require for sales and enrollment calls, all retrievable by name and by date rather than scattered across a phone, an inbox, a paper folder, and a vendor portal.
